caption_en: Zagreb grew from two towns on two neighbouring hills: Gradec in the west and Kaptol in the east.
caption_sv: Zagreb je nastao od dvaju naselja na dva susjedna brežuljka: Gradeca na zapadu i Kaptola na istoku.

caption_en: Kaptol was the bishop's town. The Diocese of Zagreb was founded here in 1094.
caption_sv: Kaptol je bio biskupov grad. Zagrebačka biskupija ovdje je osnovana 1094.

caption_en: In 1242 King Béla IV made Gradec a free royal city with the Golden Bull.
caption_sv: Kralj Bela IV. proglasio je 1242. Gradec slobodnim kraljevskim gradom Zlatnom bulom.

caption_en: The citizens built walls and towers, finished by 1266. Lotrščak tower guarded the southern gate.
caption_sv: Građani su podigli zidine i kule, dovršene do 1266. Kula Lotrščak čuvala je južna gradska vrata.

caption_en: Between the hills ran the Medveščak stream, where Tkalčićeva street is today. In 1667 the two towns clashed over a bridge across it.
caption_sv: Između brda tekao je potok Medveščak, gdje je danas Tkalčićeva ulica. Godine 1667. dva su se grada sukobila oko mosta preko njega.

caption_en: The Stone Gate is the only one of the four town gates still standing. It took its present form in 1760.
caption_sv: Kamenita vrata jedina su sačuvana od četiriju gradskih vrata. Današnji oblik dobila su 1760.
sources: Gornji grad; Kamenita vrata (hr); landmark card
photo_caption_en: The Stone Gate from the Upper Town side

caption_en: In 1850 Gradec, Kaptol and the settlements around them were joined into one city: Zagreb.
caption_sv: Godine 1850. Gradec, Kaptol i okolna naselja spojeni su u jedan grad: Zagreb.

caption_en: From the two hills the city spread south across the plain, towards the Sava.
caption_sv: S dvaju brda grad se širio na jug preko ravnice, prema Savi.
